#2143. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

#2142. Man Utd told £50m offer could tempt Fulham to sell highly rated teenager

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United could face an expensive battle to sign Fulham youngster Josh King, with offers exceeding £50million potentially enough to persuade the London club to consider a sale.

The 19-year-old has attracted attention with his performances this season, despite Fulham’s difficult results.

Manchester United are among several clubs monitoring his progress, alongside Liverpool, Arsenal, Borussia Dortmund and Barcelona.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, Pete O’Rourke explained that King’s growing reputation has put him on the radar of several major clubs.

“Josh King will be on the radar for a number of clubs because of his performances for Fulham so far this season,” O’Rourke said.

“It’s not just Liverpool, there’s been talk of the likes of Manchester United, Arsenal, Borussia Dortmund and even Barcelona looking at Josh King.”

Fulham are not actively planning to let the teenager leave in the near future as he is under contract until 2029. The contract length gives Fulham an upper hand, while interest from multiple clubs indicates a concession is not expected.

“Fulham are not planning for any early departure for Josh King. He is still under contract until 2029, and obviously they’ll want to keep him.”

The reporter also pointed to Fulham’s league position as a factor that could influence their decision. If they become embroiled in a relegation battle, losing one of their best performers would be a major risk.

“If Manchester United or any other club wanted to make an offer, he’s going to be worth in excess of £50million probably right now.”

#2141. Middlesbrough missed 'ridiculous' Ipswich Town transfer - Brighton deal has made them forget

It has been an outstanding start to the season for Middlesbrough in the Championship.

After an eventful end to last season that culminated in defeat to Hull City in the play-off final, Middlesbrough are looking to bounce back from their Wembley heartbreak, and they are among the early Championship front-runners this campaign.

Middlesbrough invested heavily in their squad this summer as owner Steve Gibson provided head coach Kim Hellberg with strong backing in the transfer market, with striker Will Lankshear becoming the club's marquee signing when he joined from Tottenham Hotspur for an initial fee of around £10 million, plus a further £10 million in add-ons.

However, Lankshear was not Boro's only big money addition, with the likes of Radek Vitek, Ashley Phillips, Max Arfsten, Sebastian Berhalter, Rokas Pukstas and Kyle Joseph also arriving for significant fees, and, so far, their bold squad rebuild is having the desired effect.

It was a disappointing week for Boro as they followed up their midweek defeat at Wrexham with an underwhelming 0-0 draw at Watford on Saturday, but while the Teesside outfit were knocked off top spot by Birmingham City on goal difference, they remain in second place heading into the November international break.

Of course, there is still a long way to go, and there will likely be plenty of twists and turns to come, but Boro will be optimistic that this will finally be the year they secure their return to the Premier League.

It is fair to say that Middlesbrough's summer transfer business caught the eye, but it seems they may have been plotting even more ambitious deals, with Ipswich Town winger Jack Clarke said to have been one name on their radar.

Despite often being used from the bench, Clarke scored an impressive 16 goals and provided two assists in 46 appearances for the Tractor Boys last season as they won automatic promotion from the Championship, and Boro were reportedly eyeing a surprise loan move for the 25-year-old in the closing stages of the summer window.

The links with Clarke were greeted with approval from FLW's Middlesbrough fan pundit Liam Day, who revealed that the Ipswich star was his dream summer transfer target, even if he had doubts over whether a deal was realistic.

"I think just because he's been linked and can somewhat be seen as maybe a small little option, I think Jack Clarke would be my dream signing before the end of the window," Liam told FLW in August.

"I think he's skilful, I think he's one of the best players in the Championship whenever he's in it, and I really hope Boro can try and get that one done.

"Do I think it's realistic? Probably not. I think Ipswich will keep hold of him. And even if he did go out on loan, you'd have half the Championship after him. So it wouldn't be an easy one for Boro to get done.

"But you know, we've seen weirder transfers, we've seen crazier transfers, and I hope it's one that we can get done, because it's in a position we very desperately need.

"I think it'd be a ridiculous signing for any Championship team."

Clarke has proven to be something of a cheat code in the Championship over the years, so it is easy to see why he was on Middlesbrough's summer wishlist, but it is no surprise that they were unable to get a deal over the line for the winger.

While he has continued to be deployed mainly as a substitute by new manager Gary O'Neil, Clarke has scored two goals and registered three assists in 11 appearances for Ipswich this season during what has been a competitive start to life back in the Premier League for the Suffolk side.

However, Boro are unlikely to be watching Clarke in the top flight with too much envy thanks to the form of Amario Cozier-Duberry, who has starred since arriving at the Riverside Stadium on a season-long loan from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer.

Cozier-Duberry scored 10 goals and provided 13 assists in 41 games to help Bolton Wanderers to promotion from League One via the play-offs last season, and he has seamlessly made the step up to the Championship with Boro.

The 21-year-old has netted three goals and registered five assists in his first 11 appearances for Boro, and he has arguably been a huge upgrade on the club's top scorer from last season, Morgan Whittaker, who departed for MLS side Colorado Rapids in September for a fee of $10.7 million (£7.9 million).

With Cozier-Duberry providing a constant threat on the right, Boro are currently the third-highest scorers in the Championship behind West Ham United and Norwich City, having bagged 30 goals in their opening 15 games.

Would Jack Clarke have been a better signing for Middlesbrough than Amario Cozier-Duberry? Tell us in the comments below!

Hellberg may still wonder what could have been if he had Clarke on the opposite flank, but Tommy Conway and Jeremy Sarmiento have performed well on the left this season, and Cozier-Duberry's exploits will certainly have softened the blow of missing out on the ex-Sunderland man.

#2140. Senegal Knockout Tie Gives Chelsea A Double Xabi Alonso Audit

Chelsea’s World Cup watch has moved beyond simple minutes management.

Senegal’s Round-of-32 meeting with Belgium now gives Xabi Alonso a live read on two very different development tracks.

Nicolas Jackson’s attacking authority is the immediate question. Mamadou Sarr’s defensive readiness is the longer-term one.

Chelsea confirmed that Senegal kept their knockout hopes alive with a 5-0 win over Iraq, with Jackson featuring from the bench.

Senegal have since moved into the knockouts, where they face Belgium in Seattle on Wednesday 1 July.

Jackson and Sarr travel into that game with contrasting club questions attached. Both still carry clear Chelsea relevance.

Sarr has not been the loudest Chelsea story of the tournament.

That may actually make this test more useful.

The 20-year-old is still moving through the awkward stage between prospect, squad option and saleable BlueCo asset.

Knockout football against Belgium can sharpen that picture quickly.

The timing is awkward in the best possible way for Chelsea. Alonso steps into a squad with expensive centre-backs, academy-trained options and a board still comfortable using the market aggressively.

A disciplined Sarr performance would not end that search. It would give the recruitment team a stronger internal benchmark before committing another major fee.

Chelsea need defenders who can hold a high line, cover wide channels and still pass through pressure. Belgium should ask those questions more directly than most group-stage opponents.

The context matters. Chelsea’s recall note recorded that Sarr returned from Strasbourg after 18 appearances across Ligue 1 and the Conference League.

The club also noted that he had already earned his first Senegal cap.

That is a different profile from an academy player being carried by reputation alone.

There is a statistical base behind the interest too. When Chelsea completed the deal, beIN SPORTS noted that Sarr made 27 Ligue 1 appearances in his first Strasbourg season.

He helped them keep 10 clean sheets. He also produced a team-high 20 blocks and made 25 interceptions.

Those numbers explain why this Belgium game is not just a sentimental World Cup subplot.

Alonso’s Chelsea defence is already crowded with Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and external targets still orbiting the plan.

ReadChelsea has already looked at why Colwill’s recovery story gives Alonso a defensive test. Sarr’s value is different.

He is still being evaluated as a physical, long-range defensive project.

Jackson’s role changes the editorial weight of the tie.

Chelsea’s striker picture has been messy for long enough. Any high-pressure international performance now carries wider meaning.

ReadChelsea has already framed the forward’s tournament as a live Senegal striker audit for Chelsea.

Belgium should stress both Chelsea questions at once.

Jackson has to offer penalty-box threat and transition security. Sarr, if trusted, has to defend space against a technically cleaner opponent.

He also has to show whether his recovery pace and frame translate under tournament pressure.

Sarr’s own mentality profile is worth noting. In a Chelsea World Cup Q&A, he named Lionel Messi, Sadio Mane and Paul Pogba as his tournament heroes.

His answer on Pogba focused on leadership and group mentality.

That lands neatly with the exact question Chelsea now need answered. Is there enough presence to go with the physical tools?

This is why Belgium feels like a pathway check rather than a routine World Cup watch item.

Chelsea do not need Sarr to solve the defence in July. They need clearer evidence on whether he belongs in Alonso’s first pre-season group.

He could need another loan. He could also become part of the club’s centre-back market arithmetic.

For Jackson, the question is more immediate. For Sarr, it is more structural.

Together, Senegal’s knockout tie gives Chelsea a rare clean look at two players on opposite ends of the same squad-building argument.

Who can help now, and who is worth protecting for later?

#2139. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2138. Michael Olise Gives Chelsea A Hard Xabi Alonso Wide-Player Benchmark

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

That should land at Cobham as more than a wistful what-if.

Bavarian Football Works relayed comments from former Chelsea and France winger Florent Malouda, who described the Bayern Munich forward as a live Ballon d’Or contender if France turn their World Cup run into silverware.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

Bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

That matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

This is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any new wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

He is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

#2137. Wolves can solve £12.7m transfer issue with Cardiff City star who is ‘different’

Wolves have had a strong Championship season so far, with Cesar Peixoto’s side currently fourth in the table, just one point off top spot.

There was a big expectation at Molineux going into the new season, and whilst the board didn’t deliver on the major squad overhaul that they promised, there’s no denying Peixoto has a talented group.

All connected to Wolves will believe there is enough in the ranks to win promotion, although the first few months of the campaign have also shown that a few glaring issues need to be addressed in the January window.

For most fans, there are two priority positions for the recruitment team to target in the New Year - a winger and a striker.

Whilst you can have some sympathy for Wolves’ striker situation due to the serious knee injury that Raul Jimenez suffered, the reality is that none of the wingers at Peixoto's disposal are truly convincing right now.

Rodrigo Gomes falls into that category, even if there is a lot to like about the Portugal U21 international in terms of his energy and enthusiasm.

However, all attacking players are judged on their end product, and Gomes has managed just two goals and one assist in 11 games, and both of those strikes came in the same game.

At 23, you would’ve expected Gomes to be doing more to deliver on his undoubted potential. There was a feeling that he could have benefited from Wolves’ relegation with a more prominent role, but, at this stage, he has failed to take that opportunity.

It would be unfair to single out Gomes, as all the wingers at Molineux are not hitting the numbers that Peixoto would want.

There's very little between the top six in the Championship right now - but who's going up to the Premier League according to Don Goodman?

Mateus Mane and Rafiki Said are yet to find the net, and the duo only have one assist apiece so far this season, although the Comoros international has done reasonably well since returning to fitness.

Jean-Ricner Bellegarde has operated out wide at times, but he looks uncomfortable, and he is another that has a poor goal return, with Bertrand Traore yet to feature in the Championship due to injury.

Only Fer Lopez is producing in terms of goals and assists, and even though he is capable of playing from the right, he prefers to start in the middle.

Therefore, a quick direct winger is needed to improve the balance of the squad, and to make Wolves more ruthless going forward.

January is a notoriously difficult month for clubs, and it will be no different for Wolves as they seek attacking reinforcements.

With promotion the aim, Wanderers must try to bring in players that can hit the ground running, so it would make sense to go for those with Championship experience.

And, one man who could help Peixoto is Ollie Tanner, with the Cardiff winger having enjoyed a productive campaign so far for the Bluebirds.

A return of three goals and four assists is a total that only Lopez beats at Wolves, which shows just how well he has done.

More importantly, Tanner has all the qualities that Peixoto wants from his winger. He will hug the right touchline, he is direct, he has pace, and he looks to beat his man at every chance, and was something of an assist-machine by setting up 12 goals from just 28 League One appearances as the Bluebirds finished second in League One last time out.

Plus, he is also capable of going down the outside to put a cross in, or cut inside onto his left to have a shot.

Tanner’s talent has been known for years, which is why he has been likened to Gareth Bale in the past, but it took time for the 24-year-old to justify that hype.

Obviously, those comparisons still seem a long way off, but there’s no doubt that Brian Barry-Murphy’s appointment has helped Tanner’s career, with the Irishman having previously claimed that the ex-Lewes man is ‘different’ with what he can do.

Wolves need someone who can help them achieve their objective of winning promotion, but they won’t want to sign a player that they would just have to discard if they did go up.

But, there will be a belief that Tanner could make his mark in the top flight, so he could be seen as a long-term solution for the Midlands outfit.

There are obviously areas of Tanner’s game that he must improve, but he has all the tools to cause even the better defenders problems due to his pace, power and ability to go both ways.

Would Ollie Tanner be a good signing for Wolves? Let us know in the comments below.

There is evidence that his decision making and composure have developed in the past 18 months, and, when you see Tanner play, you get the feeling that he still has levels to go in his game.

It’s going to be difficult to convince Cardiff to sell Tanner in January, but Wolves may have the financial muscle to tempt the Bluebirds, and if they could reach an agreement, it may turn out to be a shrewd move for the Championship high-flyers.

#2136. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

#2135. Chelsea Could Claim Share of £164m Compensation

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund new signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad. He suffered an ankle injury during Tuesday’s qualifier against Kazakhstan at Molineux. The Chelsea winger left the ground on crutches. He has returned to Stamford Bridge, where the Jamie Gittens injury will now be assessed by the club’s medical staff.

Gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. He did not take any further part in the match. England have been careful not to overstate the issue and no further reports have come out further.

The 21-year-old struggled to put weight on the affected ankle and was seen limping around Molineux after full time. That prompted an immediate release back to his club, rather than any attempt to assess him further in camp.

England Under-21 boss Lee Carsley addressed the injury directly after the game. He confirmed the nature of the knock and the decision to send Gittens home.

“Jamie got a kick on his ankle,” Carsley said after the match. “We never take any risks. With the age of these players, we don’t ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back.”

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

“Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his big summer move.

Alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

Chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

Given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.

#2132. 'He needs to do better' - £7m Middlesbrough ace sent transfer warning that will interest Man Utd

Middlesbrough have made a strong start to the season through this period up to the November international break.

The Teesside outfit lost in the play-offs last year, and are hoping to go one step further this campaign and earn their place back in the Premier League.

By the end of the term, Boro will have reached 10 years without top flight football, with their last stint at that level coming to an end in 2017.

However, Kim Hellberg’s side have gone into the break off the back of a disappointing 2-0 loss to Wrexham and a 0-0 draw against Watford.

These results have seen them lose their lead at the top of the table, falling behind Birmingham City due to an inferior goal difference.

And Radek Vitek’s mistake in the defeat to the Red Dragons has led to increased scrutiny on the goalkeeper after he joined the club from Manchester United in the summer.

When asked about Vitek’s mistake, and his general performance levels, FLW’s Middlesbrough fan pundit Liam Day claimed that he does have to improve, as he hasn’t been as good for the team as expected.

He is confused why the Czech shot-stopper is performing worse in a better team compared to his loan stint with Bristol City last season, where he was a standout performer.

“Vitek’s obviously had a very, very tough start to his Boro career, and it is quite obvious that he’s not been worth the money that we’ve paid so far,” Day told Football League World.

Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg has reacted to reports linking him with the job at Premier League outfit Crystal Palace

“Sol Brynn really disappointed me last season.

“Obviously, I would say one of the main causes of us not being in the Premier League, to be completely honest with you.

“So, goalkeeper was a main priority and I can see why we went for Vitek.

“You look at last season, and you look at what he’s doing for us, and I’m really confused why the fall-off has happened.

“He’s playing in a better team, we concede less chances, and yet he’s struggling to do anything with the ones he is conceding.

“He’s not made many saves, and it is really just quite confusing.

“And that Wrexham one midweek was a really weird one, just went straight through him.

Vitek spent last season on loan at Bristol City, where he kept 12 clean sheets from 41 appearances in the Championship, conceding on 54 occasions.

Middlesbrough agreed a deal with Man United that involved an initial £7 million fee, with add-ons and a sell-on clause also involved in the arrangement.

The goalkeeper signed a five-year deal, keeping him at the Riverside until June 2031.

Kieffer Moore’s tame shot from outside the box was spilled by Vitek, which allowed George Thomason to pounce to open the scoring against Boro from a tight angle last week.

And it went from bad to worse for the 23-year-old, who saw Ollie Rathbone’s 84th minute strike go through his legs to make it 2-0 to the Red Dragons.

Vitek has a goals prevented per 90 of -0.20 so far this season, suggesting he is letting in more goals than he should based on the quality of chances conceded (all stats from Fotmob).

Next up for Boro is a home clash against the goalkeeper’s former club Bristol City on 21 November in a 3pm kick-off.

It’s still early days for Vitek’s time at Middlesbrough, as he is being judged off of 15 games on a five-year contract.

However, it’s clear after the Wrexham defeat that he does need to improve his standard if he is to retain his position in the team long-term.

Will Radek Vitek turn his form around for Middlesbrough? Comment your opinion below

Middlesbrough are targeting automatic promotion to the Premier League, and if he wants to be a part of that future then he has to be performing more to the level he set while at Bristol City.

Fortunately for him, this might just be a particularly poor spell, and perhaps the break now will allow him to reset mentally and get back to his best when the league returns later this month.

#2131. Manu Koné: Roma slap £86m price tag on Chelsea target

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

“There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of important players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable with a recurring shin problem, while Patrick Dorgu is expected to be out until late November. Manuel Ugarte is recovering from knee surgery, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt with a back problem.

There is better news regarding Matthijs de Ligt, who could return to contention. Leny Yoro is also available for selection despite his Champions League suspension.

The match takes place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18. Kick-off is scheduled for 2 pm BST (1pm GMT).

UK viewers can watch the game live on Sky Sports Main Event, with coverage beginning at 1 pm BST.

#2128. Birmingham City have one condition for January transfer plans, John Murtough confirms

Birmingham City's new director of football, John Murtough, has outlined exactly what supporters at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park are likely to expect ahead of the upcoming January transfer window.

The 56-year-old was recently installed into said role in B9 after a long-standing search for the successor of Craig Gardner, with Blues currently top of the Championship.

Throughout Knighthead Capital Management's ownership of the club, ambition has been a key buzzword, and that has often been backed up by activity in the transfer market.

Birmingham sent shockwaves through the footballing world two summers ago when they broke their transfer record by luring Jay Stansfield back to St. Andrew's for in excess of £15m on a seven-year contract.

It remains to be seen what position Chris Davies' side find themselves in come January, with there bound to be a focus on potential arrivals to aid a promotion bid.

Last summer saw Birmingham recruit as many as 14 new signings after a record-breaking season in League One, with many outsiders firmly holding the belief that Davies' squad were strong enough to finish inside the Championship's play-off places for the first time since 2012.

However, many of those additions flattered to deceive, namely big-money striker, Kyogo Furuhashi, who was one of five senior departees this summer.

The NFL icon severed his ties with the Championship leaders on Monday evening

With Davies refining his tactical approach, only seven transfers were made this summer, of which two were already at the club last season in the form of James Beadle and Jhon Solis, whilst Max Bird and Liam Millar, in particular, have made immediate impressions.

Murtough has overseen hierarchical roles at Everton, Fulham, Coventry City and Manchester United, during which Cristiano Ronaldo returned to Old Trafford, and will now be tasked with aiding the recruitment process at St. Andrew's.

It remains to be seen who will become available to the Championship promotion hopefuls in January, but during an in-house interview, the experienced figure outlined exactly what staff behind-the-scenes will be looking at, as the winter window is notoriously difficult for doing business in.

"January, I see as a window where there potentially is opportunities," Murtough explained.

"We're aware of what players are out there. It may be sometimes difficult in actually getting the players that we want. They're usually more available in the summer windows.

"But, if an opportunity becomes available in January which we think can strengthen the squad, and it fits within the model that we're building, I'm sure we'll be ready and able to react to that," he added.

"One of the things we'll be looking for is building towards the summer. But, if something comes available and it fits within the plan that we're working towards, we'll be ready to react."

#2127. Jamie Carragher names Man Utd Star who impressed him against Leeds

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

“But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”

Leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”

The result may feel like another opportunity missed for Carrick, but Maguire’s performance gave United something positive to take away from Elland Road.

Brazil’s coaching staff confirmed the withdrawal, pointing to the same knee issue that kept him out of the derby. Chelsea have not set a firm return date for Joao Pedro, leaving supporters to wait for further updates during the international break.

#2125. Pep Guardiola Speaks Out as Man City Found Guilty of 114 Charges

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 financial charges, the Premier League has confirmed. The verdict follows an eight-week hearing that opened almost two years ago. It closes one of the most significant disciplinary cases in the competition’s history.

Former head coach Pep Guardiola has already broken his silence. Reaction to the Pep Guardiola Man City charges verdict is spreading fast across the division, with Chelsea among the clubs watching closely.

Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016 and turned them into the dominant force in English football. He left his post earlier this summer, with the club having already worked through plans to replace Pep Guardiola at City.

His exit means he holds no formal role at the Etihad. Yet he moved quickly to make his loyalty clear once the ruling landed. According to the football.london report that first carried his statement, Guardiola posted directly to his supporters.

“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

The Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. Every point City may have gained through breaches has a knock on effect further down the table.

Most top flight clubs including Chelsea are now pushing for City to face relegation as a consequence of the verdict. Some are reported to be weighing up legal action of their own. Guardiola has spoken about Chelsea before, including Guardiola’s previous comments on Chelsea. This latest statement fits a pattern of public backing for Manchester City, despite the criticism now directed at the club.

For Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

Manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.

#2124. Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

#2123. Tony Pulis reveals 'massive difference' that has transformed Stoke City

Stoke City head into the international break in third place, level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough at the top, and had you told any Potters fan that after the first three games this season, they would have laughed.

Indeed, Stoke began the Championship campaign in miserable form, suffering defeats to each of Swansea City, Southampton, and Wolverhampton Wanderers, as the pressure piled on manager Mark Robins, especially after a poor second half to last season.

The departure of Sorba Thomas on deadline day and subsequent switch to a 3-4-2-1 shape has, much to the disbelief of many, transformed the Potters' form, as no team in the division has picked up more points than Stoke since the beginning of September, winning nine, drawing two, and losing once.

Numerous factors can be pointed to Stoke's recent success, but few are better-placed to assess the Potters' recent revival than former boss and fan favourite, Tony Pulis.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

Welsh boss Pulis enjoyed two separate spells in charge of Stoke, the first between 2002 and 2005, and the next, most notably, between 2006 and 2013, where he guided the Potters to the Premier League, established them in the top flight, took them to an FA Cup final, and the latter stages of the Europa League.

Spells with Crystal Palace, West Bromwich Albion, Middlesbrough, and Sheffield Wednesday would follow before bringing an end to his managerial days in 2020, though it was his time at the bet365 Stadium, then known as the Britannia Stadium, that he is best known for.

Speaking with former Wolverhampton Wanderers boss Mick McCarthy on 'The Managers' podcast, Pulis revealed his thoughts on Stoke's upturn in form, saying: "At the beginning of the season, they had a poor start, and there were real question marks about whether they would keep Mark [Robins].

"I think the last three or four players they have recruited have made a massive difference to the team, and since those players have come in, those fortunes have changed.

"They've got momentum now, and when they get momentum at that football club, it's a very, very difficult place to go to.

"The crowds will increase, they'll get behind the team, they can see improvement, and it will be a damn difficult place to go and win. And if Mark can keep that going, it will be absolutely fantastic."

Stoke were quick to confirm the likes of Josh Griffiths, Ethan Galbraith, Djibril Soumare, Luke Graham, and Svante Ingelsson in the summer window, as the likes of George Hirst, Ben Johnson, Justin Devenny, Luca Bombino, and Jack McGlynn followed.

Galbraith, Soumare, Graham, Johnson, and McGlynn, in particular, have each proven to be wonderful additions to the club, with each having a positive impact on the squad since their arrivals.

Without Galbraith dictating games, Soumare breaking up play, Graham leading from the back, Johnson getting up and down the right flank, and McGlynn's magic left foot, Stoke would be nowhere near the Championship top two right now, as Pulis' assessment is bang on the money.

What have you made of Stoke's season so far? Is Pulis' assessment correct, or would you disagree with the Welshman? Share your thoughts below!

As we head into the next international break, the mood around Stoke right now is as good as it has been in years, with the Potters most recently breaking a record dating back to 1947 by recording five away wins on the spin.

Without the impact of his summer arrivals, this would not have been possible, and Robins almost certainly would have been without a job.

However, Stoke are flying right now, but mustn't rest on their laurels, as Robins must continue to demand more from his summer cohort, as well as pre-existing players in the squad, as something special could be happening at the bet365 Stadium this year.

#2122. Alex Scott Chelsea Transfer Blocked as Bournemouth Eye January Stay

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January. That is according to reports from the Daily Mail and BBC Sport. Both outlets say the Cherries want to keep their young midfielder as they fight to protect their Premier League status this season.

Chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old. Reports suggest the Blues have already tested Bournemouth’s resolve with a bid worth close to £64 million. Bournemouth have given no indication they are willing to negotiate. Scott, the reports say, simply is not for sale this winter.

Reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter. The club’s hierarchy reportedly view Scott as central to their survival plan, wary of leaning on new signings mid-season rather than trusting the squad they already have.

A fee of around £64 million, first reported by Football London, is said to have been offered by Chelsea during recent discussions.

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023. He has quickly become one of the most sought-after young midfielders in English football. Interest from a club the size of Chelsea shows how far his reputation has grown, though Bournemouth’s stance makes a January move increasingly unlikely.

Scott’s rise has been underlined by his first appearance for England. He came off the bench for a 20-minute cameo as Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League. The manager praised him afterwards.

“Alex Scott has maybe one of the best performances in midfield in the Premier League since the start with Bournemouth.”

“Individually he’s one of the outstanding midfielders so he clearly deserves to be with us.”

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”

That praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

Chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

The prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

#2121. Rio Ferdinand disappointed Man Utd didn’t sign midfielder better than Elliot Anderson

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand said.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”

#2120. "I can't see Southampton doing it" - West Ham transfer plea made for Aaron Ramsdale

Despite being a former Championship-winning goalkeeper, Mads Hermansen hasn't earned any glory back in the division at West Ham United, and some Hammers fans want to see him replaced altogether.

The Dane was solid for the London Stadium-based side in the Premier League, replacing Alphonse Areola when Nuno came in and keeping seven clean sheets in 18 league games.

So far this season, though, he's conceded over four more than his expected goals against tally suggests he should have, with a save percentage of just 54%. West Ham fans were heard booing his every touch at Blackburn Rovers, where Scott Parker's side fell to a third defeat in four league games.

Unfortunately, though, with Areola suffering an injury in the warm-up at Ewood Park, Hermansen seems to be Parker's only senior option in between the sticks until January at least, when it's almost universally agreed that a new keeper will be on the shopping list.

Aaron Ramsdale's name has been floated around Hammers fans as a potential January recruit, with the 28-year-old firmly third-choice at St Mary's following a dud loan spell at Newcastle United last season.

Ramsdale has played at the top level for the majority of his career, but his stock has fallen so far after leaving Arsenal for the South Coast that the ex-England international will be looking anywhere to help revive it.

FLW's West Ham fan pundit, Ryan Horn, hopes that his side looks for a goalkeeper in January, and wouldn't mind seeing Ramsdale pursued. They're arguably the only Championship side that could afford his top-flight-level wages, and he could rediscover some form back in the capital.

"We should be looking to bring in a keeper, and I wouldn't mind Ramsdale," he said. "I know he's had issues in the past, like at Arsenal and in the past couple of years, but I'd definitely give him a go."

Would you like to see Aaron Ramsdale at the London Stadium, Hammers fans? Let us know in the comments.

Horn did express some doubt, though, about whether Southampton would want to send Ramsdale to the London Stadium, as that could strengthen a promotion rival, even if the fan pundit admits his side doesn't look like challenging for the top two just yet.

The 28-year-old may be far from first choice at St Mary's, but there's no doubt about the quality of the keeper if he can revive his career elsewhere. Perhaps a move to West Ham would be too risky for them.

"Hopefully we can do a deal, but I can't see Southampton doing it," he explained. "I don't think they'd want to strengthen a promotion rival. As much as we don't look like one at the moment, I do feel that we'll get there."

In the meantime, though, Horn hopes that, given Hermansen's poor form, Scott Parker will take a chance on young goalkeeper Finley Herrick, who has just three appearances for West Ham, none of which have come in league action.

With Areola out injured, the fan pundit doesn't want it to feel that Parker has no choice over whom to play, as he doesn't feel that the Dane has done enough to warrant starts.

"I would bring Ramsdale in, try and move Hermansen on, and at the moment, with Areola out injured, I would like to see Herrick get game time," the fan pundit continued.

"You can't keep rewarding Hermansen with game time when he isn't putting the performances in. What would that show to our younger players? Just because you may be the best on paper, shouldn't mean that you get to come in and have game time every week.

"I'd rather Parker take the risk and reward game time to players who deserve it."

It would be a risk, giving Herrick minutes, given his lack of senior experience. However, with some West Ham fans losing complete faith in Hermansen, perhaps it would be wise to take the 26-year-old out of the firing line for a week or so.

If Herrick performs well in the meantime, then perhaps he'd be worthy of a more extended period in between the sticks.

On the Ramsdale move, Southampton are in a difficult situation. The 28-year-old would be on such large wages that it would be wise to move him on and not have to pay him each week to not play.

However, very few clubs would be open to paying what Saints, or Ramsdale himself, may want for the goalkeeper. Yes, the majority of his career has been at Premier League level, but he's been relegated from the division three times.

#2119. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2117. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.
