#1985. Liverpool: Hungary confirm "last-minute" Dominik Szoboszlai decision in new injury update

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 10:12

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will remain with the Hungary national team following medical examinations, the Magyars have announced.

The 26-year-old arrived for the November international break carrying a knee injury, which he sustained in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola admitted at full time that Szoboszlai was not feeling 100%, although the former RB Leipzig man nevertheless joined up with his compatriots for the UEFA Nations League.

Hungary issued a statement on Monday morning announcing that Szoboszlai would undergo further medical tests on his knee sprain, which have now been completed, and he will not be sent back to Kirkby.

However, in a fresh update on Tuesday, Hungary also conceded that they are unlikely to make any decisions on Szoboszlai's involvement until the very last minute.

"Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible," the statement read.

"However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute."

Hungary face Georgia in their penultimate Nations League group-stage game on Saturday, before also taking on Northern Ireland next Tuesday in League B Group 2.

The Magyars currently sit second in the group with seven points from four games, one point adrift of leaders Northern Ireland in top spot, which guarantees promotion to League A.

Hungary's second-placed ranking would see Szoboszlai's side advance to the promotion playoffs, where they would meet a third or fourth-placed team from League A for the right to progress to the top tier.

Szoboszlai came back from the September/October international break with a hamstring injury, which he then exacerbated against Brentford, causing him to miss five games in total for Liverpool so far this season.

As Hungary are vying for League A promotion, and Szoboszlai is arguably their most important player, the Magyars' decision to keep the midfielder around for now is both understandable and defensible.

Liverpool fans will no doubt want the midfielder to withdraw, return to Merseyside and enjoy a complete rest over the international break, and that scenario could still occur if his knee issue flares up over the coming days.

However, Szoboszlai should also do everything in his power to make himself available for his country, thereby forcing Liverpool fans to watch on anxiously over the next week.

#1981. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:07 EST, 7 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

#1980. 'Influential' former Scottish Premiership boss amongst favourites for major EPL job amid 'wrong time' warning

Former Motherwell head coach Jens Berthel Askou has emerged as a leading candidate for a vacant role at a top English Premier League club just 173 days after leaving Fir Park.

Berthel Askou, 44, made a major impact in his sole season at Motherwell last year, helping the club qualify for European football, while setting a new club record for the most clean sheets in a single season during an impressive 2025–26 campaign.

His success in the Scottish Premiership saw him linked to numerous top jobs, with Celtic heavily reported to be interested in his services, before Ligue 1 outfit Toulouse swooped in to lure the Danish manager across the channel just days after Motherwell’s season came to an end.

Speaking last month, Stephen Welsh hailed the impact the boss had on his career after the ex-Motherwell loanee made his Scotland debut last month, saying he was "the biggest influence on my career by a distance.”

Just ten games into his spell at Stadium de Toulouse, Berthel Askou’s reputation has continued to flourish after a steady start to his time in France, with his side sitting 12th in Ligue 1, and he has now been understood to have caught the attention of Conference League champions Crystal Palace, who are understood to be on the verge of sacking Pierre Sage after a difficult start to the season at Selhurst Park.

The former RC Lens manager replaced Oliver Glasner in the summer, but is currently bottom of the English Premier League, having won just two of their opening 10 league games. While Sage’s departure has yet to be formally confirmed, reports say he has effectively been dismissed by Crystal Palace after the 3–1 home defeat to Liverpool at the weekend, with the club just finalising compensation terms.

Former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur manager Thomas Frank has been installed as the leading candidate to replace the outgoing Frenchman, Berthel Askou has emerged as a manager contender for the role, with reports claiming the Eagles are ready to cast their net far and wide to find a manager that can drag them out of the relegation mire.

Despite being installed as the joint second favourite for the Selhurst Park role alongside Sean Dyche at 11/2 (Betfair), the ex-Motherwell boss has been told to turn down any approach by former Celtic striker and current TV pundit Chris Sutton. The 53-year-old believes the club’s immediate threat of relegation could see him deviate away from his footballing principles and has warned him that the time is wrong for a move to the English Premier League.

"It's the wrong time for him to go in," Sutton told BBC. "In terms of the way he wants to play and how expansive he is, I don't think it's the right move for him or for Palace when you are a quarter of a way through the season. If you brought him in over the summer and he has time to build then it would work, but you have the likes of Sean Dyche who is ready to go in and organise. I wouldn't want to see Berthel Askou go in and rip up the way he works just to keep Palace in the Premier League."

#1979. Germany squad: Five players to watch under Jurgen Klopp this month including 17-year-old wunderkind

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 10:20

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has drastically trimmed his squad ahead of two crucial UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands during the November international break.

Facing a must-win double-header, Die Mannschaft are in danger of failing to qualify for the quarter-finals as they currently sit third in League A Group C, three points behind both of their upcoming opponents.

Germany will first travel to Belgrade to face Serbia on Friday, before returning home to host the Netherlands in a blockbuster clash at the Olympiastadion in Berlin next Monday.

From history-making teenage playmakers to reborn Bundesliga stars and Premier League luminaries, Klopp's 24-man squad is a fascinating blend of elite experience and explosive youth.

These two crunch matches present the ultimate stage for several international hopefuls to cement their place under Klopp, and here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at five Germany players to watch out for during this month's international break.

The surprise inclusion to Klopp’s latest squad is Borussia Monchengladbach’s wunderkind Wael Mohya, who has earned his first-ever senior call-up for Germany ahead of his 18th birthday next month.

The 2008 Mettmann-born starlet, who is of Moroccan descent through his parents, broke into Monchengladbach’s senior team midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since been linked with the likes of Bayern and Liverpool in recent months, having developed into an increasingly influential figure under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all nine Bundesliga games as well as two DFB-Pokal matches.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in back-to-back matches last month, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 victory over Stuttgart – Monchengladbach’s only league win of the season to date.

The dynamic teenage attacker, comfortable operating centrally and as a winger on either flank, is blessed with superb close control and an innate ability to operate comfortably with both feet, offering Klopp a highly creative, versatile midfield weapon.

Mohya, who has received eight Germany youth caps between Under-16 and Under-21 level, is undeniably one to watch this month as he bids to become the third-youngest senior international in German history and bring his fearless club form onto the Nations League stage.

An explosive start to the 2026-27 campaign by striker Niclas Fullkrug has been rewarded with a return to the Germany national team squad for the first time since September 2025.

The veteran marksman endured difficult spells at both West Ham United and AC Milan, but he is enjoying a remarkable revival on loan at Werder Bremen, where he began his career 15 years ago.

At the age of 33, Fullkrug has proven that age is just a number by plundering a ruthless nine goals in as many Bundesliga appearances so far this season, firing him to the top of the division’s scoring charts and already five clear of Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Fullkrug’s lethal aerial presence and old-school, back-to-goal physical profile offer Germany a genuine focal point with qualities that differ to both Kai Havertz and Younes Ebnoutalib who will also battle for the No.9 role under Klopp.

If Germany are to breach the backlines of Serbia and the Netherlands this month, Fullkrug's predatory instincts inside the penalty area could be paramount should he be selected to lead the line.

Having made his senior international debut under Klopp during the previous window, Koln’s crown jewel has done more than enough to maintain his place in this refined 24-man squad.

The highly-rated 20-year-old winger has seamlessly transitioned his dominant youth form into the Bundesliga, contributing to 18 goals (13 goals, five assists) in 34 top-flight matches last season to help Koln avoid relegation.

This term, El Mala has found the net five times in 10 appearances in all competitions, including a late consolation strike against Bayer Leverkusen last weekend, and his strong performances continue to be monitored by a number of Europe’s biggest clubs.

Boasting rare physical traits for a wide player at 6ft 2in, El Mala pairs raw explosive pace with clinical goalscoring instincts, and his ability to drive vertically at opposing full-backs provides a unique dynamic to a German attack that has typically favoured shorter, intricate passing combinations.

With Klopp eager to establish a permanent threat on the flanks, El Mala represents a intriguing tactical alternative for this month's double-header while the likes of Karim Adeyemi, Serge Gnabry, Leroy Sane, Chris Fuhrich, Jamie Leweling and Kevin Schade all watch on from afar.

Having initially been left out of Klopp’s squad, Ridle Baku has received a late call-up to the Germany set-up after Waldemar Anton was forced to withdraw over the weekend due to injury.

The right-back has played 12 times for a Leipzig side who sit fourth in the Bundesliga table and has chipped in with three goals, with his qualities on full display in a narrow Champions League defeat to Man City last week in which he fired home a second-half equaliser.

The 28-year-old right-back has not featured for the national team since earning his eighth cap in November last year, but this window offers a massive opportunity for him to revitalise his international career.

Baku will face stern competition for starts at right-back from Freiburg's Philipp Treu who was preferred for the previous international window and made a notable impression during his maiden Germany outing.

However, having two strong right-back options battling it out against each other would enable Klopp to continue with captain Joshua Kimmich as a central midfielder, where his tactical intelligence and elite passing range can orchestrate the play.

In the absence of injured star Jamal Musiala, Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz carries the creative burden for Klopp’s Germany side and will hope to transfer his recent form at club level onto the international stage.

Wirtz has previously come under fire for failing to make the desired impact at Liverpool, but he ranks joint-second for chances created in the Premier League so far this season (22) and has contributed to four goals in his last four top-flight appearances.

After setting up goals in wins over Brighton and Brentford, Wirtz scored and assisted in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, helping Andoni Iraola’s side climb back into the top four.

At 23 years of age, Wirtz is in fact one of the more experienced players in Klopp’s squad, as his 48 international caps is only bettered by three players (Kimmich, Havertz and Jonathan Tah).

Having captained Germany in their last Nations League match, Wirtz will be tasked with orchestrating the offensive tempo from the number 10 role as the battle for knockout qualification reaches a boiling point.

He will aim to replicate his man-of-the-match display in last month's 2-0 win over Serbia in which he scored and assisted.

#1978. Abdsami lashes home the only goal as Hassocks leave Lingfield with a sixth consecutive win

Not many who watched Hassocks thrash Lingfield 5-1 on the opening day of the campaign would have predicted the return match at Church Road would take place with the Robins sitting fourth and the hosts fifth in the Southern Combination Premier Division.

Lingfield have improved markedly over the past three months to put themselves firmly in the playoff picture - making this 1-0 victory for Hassocks one of the Robins' most impressive results of the season.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"A brilliant win," was how James Westlake described it afterwards. "This is a really hard place to come and play football. Not many teams will come here this season and not only win the game but also keep a clean sheet like we have done today."

The shutout was particularly impressive given Lingfield came into the fixture as the second-highest scorers in the league so far this season after Eastbourne United.

Ed Cooper made one outstanding double save late in the first half but Hassocks kept the home side relatively quiet other than that. It was a formidable performance defensively from the Robins.

A scrappy first half was lacking in quality on a playing surface which is more 1G than 3G. Omar Abdsami looked the most likely player to break the deadlock for Hassocks in the opening 45 minutes.

He had an early shot deflected over the bar and then drilled a low effort into the diving arms of Mac Chisholm after tall striker Jamie Wilkes badgered to win possession from a half-cleared Lewis Finney free kick.

Dan Turner struck a rasping volley just wide in-between those two Abdsami chances. Lingfield had their first real sight of goal when Gabriel Odunaike managed to get in one-on-one but could only fire a long way over the bar.

Next came that brilliant intervention from Cooper. Lingfield's 14-goal top scorer Kwesi Ntim tricked his way in from the left flank to draw a full stretch save on the angle out of Cooper.

The rebound fell kindly for Callum Corbin, who looked to have picked out the top corner with a powerful shot until Cooper somehow recovered and appeared from nowhere to push away the follow up.

At the start of the second half, the weather became almost as gloomy as the surroundings. Over to Adsami to brighten things up with a spectacular goal out of nothing on 53 minutes.

Blake pushed forward from right back and delivered a cross which was cleared only as far as Abdsami on the edge of the box.

Abdsami was surrounded by red and yellow striped shirts but took a touch, managed to wiggle into space and picked out the far corner with a sweeping shot giving Chisholm no chance.

A pretty special way for Abdsami to move onto double figures in his first full season of senior football.

Lingfield enjoyed a good spell after that in which they had plenty of the ball but could find no way through. Turner produced a fine piece of defending to clear away a cross which otherwise might have left Ntim with a tap in at the back post.

Otherwise, the Lingers' settled for wayward shooting from distance which posed more danger to home fans in the stand behind the goal than Cooper.

Having weathered the mini storm, it was Hassocks who finished the stronger. Lingfield committed more players forward in the closing stages and that left gaps for the Robins to exploit on the counter.

A tight offside call prevented Big Alex Fair from doubling the lead. Good hold up play from Liam Benson saw him slip Fair in for a clinical finish past Chisholm ruled out by the flag. The fact Fair took the decision with unusually good grace suggests the assistant made the correct call.

Fair then sent a header from a Finney corner towards the top corner. The Lingfield player on the near post did a remarkable job in heading it off the line to ensure his side remained in the tie.

Hassocks managed to get the ball back into the box where Benson was denied by a block and substitute Luke Brodie shot just wide from the rebound.

The Robins kept pushing and managed to rack up a couple more corners. Another taken by Finney was headed on target by Turner.

This time Chisholm pulled off a superb save to claw it out. Brodie retrieved possession and fed Fair to go around two defenders inside the area, only for a third to block his eventual shot.

Not that Hassocks needed a second goal. The full time whistle blew shortly after, followed by some strange scenes as the teams trooped off when one of the Lingfield coaching staff was accused of grabbing Turner's hand and biting it.

It was an unusual ending for a game which featured only one yellow card and showed little edge to it. Turner typically took it all in his stride as the Robins headed home chewing on a sixth consecutive win in all competitions.

Hassocks: Ed Cooper; Harvey Blake, Dan Turner, Liam Hendy, Joe Bull; Jamie Wilkes, Lewis Finney; Alex Fair, Omar Abdsami, Joe Turner; Liam Benson.

Subs: Darren Budd, Luke Brodie, Ruari Farrell (used), Lewis Croal, Charlie Bonwick-Adams (unused).

Starman: Harvey Blake. The whole back four were marvellous but the Hassocks captain just edged it.

#1977. Rangers loanee says 'big responsibility' taking game to new levels as ex-Ibrox hero opens up on transfer talks

Aasgaard, 24, started the campaign in the Rangers starting XI, scoring in the opening day 1-1 draw with Dundee United, but was deemed surplus to requirements shortly and was allowed to move to Lotto Park on a season-long loan deal ahead of the transfer deadline.

He initially struggled for minutes in the Belgian Pro League and was forced to make an impact off the bench. However, in recent weeks, Aasgaard has impressed in a deep-lying midfield role. Local outlets labelled him as a player who possesses "Anderlecht DNA" after an impressive last month.

“We spoke throughout the year and even at the end of the season before we finished, there were talks with Rangers,” Moore told the Daily Record. “I was speaking with my agent, and he was up at Ibrox speaking with the owner and stuff. But to be honest, it kind of stopped when Danny left.

“I think once he'd gone, it didn't make as much sense for me. I needed to take another step, to push on to try and challenge myself.”

#1974. Arsenal: Why Myles Lewis-Skelly will miss England vs. Croatia as Nations League rules explained

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 10:34, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 10:34

Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly will be unavailable for England's upcoming UEFA Nations League clash with Croatia at Wembley on Thursday evening due to suspension.

The 20-year-old was called up to Thomas Tuchel's squad for November's final two League A Group 3 games against Croatia and Spain, as the Three Lions aim to seal qualification for the quarter-finals.

England sit second in the group with nine points from four matches, six clear of third-placed Croatia, meaning they just need one point from their final two games to progress.

Lewis-Skelly featured in all four of England's contests across September and October, but he also picked up two yellow cards, both of which came against the Czech Republic.

As two bookings is enough to incur a one-game ban in the Nations League, Lewis-Skelly will sit out the visit of Croatia, before returning for the trip to Spain on Sunday.

Lewis-Skelly's presence was vital in September and October, as the Arsenal man started three of England's first four Nations League games, playing the full 90 against Czechia on matchday four.

Lewis-Skelly helped negate the impact of losing Declan Rice, but his Arsenal teammate is now fit and firing and ready to take his place alongside Elliot Anderson in midfield on Thursday evening.

Tuchel can also deploy James Garner and the uncapped Jobe Bellingham in the engine room, as well as Trent Alexander-Arnold, whose spot at right-back can be covered by the returning Djed Spence and Ben White.

Jude Bellingham could also drop into a deeper role, as all of Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze and Joshua King can function as a number 10, so England are expected to cope just fine in Lewis-Skelly's absence.

However, the older Bellingham brother will be walking a tightrope if he features on Thursday evening, as he is also just one yellow card away from incurring a Nations League ban.

The Real Madrid star was booked against Spain on matchday one, but has since managed to avoid the second yellow card that would force him onto the sidelines for one game.

Bellingham will miss the trip to Spain if he is cautioned on Thursday evening, though, but he is the only England player in the current squad at risk of a yellow-card ban for the final matchday.

Manchester City duo Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly are also on one Nations League booking apiece, but neither player will feature this month; Guehi withdrew through injury on Monday, and O'Reilly was not selected.

Yellow cards that do not result in a suspension are wiped after the quarter-finals, but the two-booking rule remains until the first two legs of the knockout stage have been completed.

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he dropped the clearest hint yet that he is heading to Real Madrid in an interview with Spanish media.

The 16-year-old sensation stunned Manchester United with a formal transfer request in September and is now on the verge of finalising his move to the Spanish capital.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet last month, with Gabriel now having secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage.

The youngster, who is currently working with a personal trainer in Madrid, practically confirmed the transfer in an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca on Friday night, admitting he had a clear preference to Real over archrivals Barcelona.

'Obviously Madrid,' Gabriel told the outlet when asked which LaLiga giant he preferred.

According to the newspaper, who expects his move to be finalised in January, Gabriel's response prompted a laugh from his father and mentor Joe O'Cearuill.

Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel poses for his interview with Spanish newspaper Marca

Gabriel is set to complete a move to Real Madrid after formally requesting to leave Old Trafford

'My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,' explained the talented youngster, who scored a hat-trick for Manchester United in the UEFA Youth League just days before submitting his transfer request.

Although Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal narrowly missed out on winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or - which was held aloft by England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane - the two LaLiga giants have long had a rich association with the award, regularly producing the world's best footballer.

While sources at United insist there has been no club-to-club contact, it appears only a matter of time before Gabriel is sporting Real Madrid's iconic all-white jersey.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

The prodigy, who was 14 when he netted twice on his debut, has also played - and scored - for Manchester United's Under-21 side.

The Red Devils were rocked in September when Gabriel and his representatives made a bombshell request to have his academy contract torn up. That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

Gabriel's dream is to win the Ballon d'Or, which was awarded this year to England's Harry Kane

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson has been the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

His father has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent and is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

#1969. England announce fresh Ezri Konsa blow as Thomas Tuchel makes change for Croatia

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 10:42, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 10:57

England have announced that Arsenal's Ezri Konsa will miss Thursday's UEFA Nations League match against Croatia, and Bournemouth's James Hill has been added to the squad.

Arsenal defender Konsa picked up a small injury in the Gunners' recent Champions League win over Slavia Prague, but he was fit enough to return against Hull City a few days later.

The 29-year-old played the full 90 minutes of that 1-0 win for the Premier League champions, the eighth time this season in the top flight that he has seen out the game.

Konsa was originally expected to start for England at Wembley on Thursday evening, but the Three Lions released a statement on Tuesday morning confirming that he was out of contention.

The former Aston Villa man has been restricted to individual training since his arrival, but he will be back with the group ahead of Sunday's finale against Spain.

"Ezri Konsa will not be in contention for Croatia at Wembley on Thursday as he continues to follow his own programme but will return to full training later this week before Sunday’s trip to Spain," England said.

A former #YoungLions players called to represent our #ThreeLions for the very first time ? ❤️ Congratulations, James Hill ? https://t.co/wc8N4KMntH

With Konsa unavailable against Croatia, Tuchel has handed a maiden senior call-up to Bournemouth's Hill, who has been a stalwart of the Cherries' squad this season.

The 24-year-old has played every minute of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign for Marco Rose's men, who have won each of their last four games against Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds United and Ipswich Town, conceding just once in the process.

Hill previously represented England at Under-20 and Under-21 level, although he only made one appearance for the latter in a 5-0 win over Kosovo in June 2022.

The centre-back is the second new addition to England's November squad, after Newcastle United's Dan Burn replaced the injured Marc Guehi on Monday, and the fourth uncapped name in the ranks alongside Josh King, Jobe Bellingham and Jason Steele.

Konsa joins a lengthy list of England defensive absentees that also includes Guehi, Harry Maguire, Trevoh Chalobah and John Stones, but Tuchel is still not short of options at the back.

With Hill and Burn added to the squad, Tuchel has five players who can function in the heart of defence, including Ben White, Jarell Quansah and Jarrad Branthwaite.

The latter two are the most likely to be given the nod on Thursday evening, as Quansah started three of England's four matches across the September/October international break, although two came as a right-back.

Branthwaite, meanwhile, came off the bench in fixtures against Spain and the Czech Republic, and the 24-year-old has started nine of Everton's 10 Premier League matches this season.

As well as Konsa, England will also be without Myles Lewis-Skelly against Croatia, whom they only need one point against to seal their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals.

#1968. Midweek magic follows weekend woe as Eastbourne Borough down Dulwich Hamlet

For Borough supporters, loyalty comes with a sou'wester and a set of waterproofs: only a week ago, after the gale-blown victory over Stanway Rovers, manager Steve King had described the conditions as "horrendous" – and this week's weather was another challenge.

The game began in drizzle and ended in sweeping rain - the sort that, in shimmering floodlights, can look almost picturesque. Almost...

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But who notices a few drips down your neck when your team is winning? Borough supporters had returned deflated from Dartford, but by the second half of Tuesday's game they were pumped up and roaring again.

Postponed from an October Saturday because of Borough's FA Cup run, the visit of Dulwich Hamlet was just a little anti-climactic. The South London club and their buoyant supporters usually travel in numbers and liven up any game - but the logistics of a Tuesday night journey to the coast are trickier.

Hamlet's own league form has been patchy this season, but they always play without fear and they enjoy nothing better than a game which starts at high pace and then gets quicker.

That was precisely how Tuesday night's action began at the Lane. After two early chances for the Sports from corner-kicks, Hamlet snatched a surprise lead in the sixth minute, with a flicked finish by David Smith just beyond the reach of home keeper Lewis Carey.

The Sports were stirred rather than shaken - and a bit indignant. Chances came and went, but Dulwich were defending deep, and the home side were caught between playing their instinctive purist football or piling forward and getting the ball any which way into the Hamlet penalty area.

Indeed, the visitors were growing in confidence, and they created chances to extend the lead: one smart Lewis Carey save and two excellent interventions, by Max Sheaf and Freddie Carter, snuffed out the openings.

A huge home shout for a penalty was waved away by the referee - but the Sports were not relying on marginal decisions as they suddenly breached the Hamlet defences.

With 25 minutes played, a deep Josh Rees cross was met at the back post by Liam Nash - in his first full game back after injury - and Darren McQueen pounced to slide in the equaliser.

Most games have a turning point and that McQueen finish turned the mood for players, manager and huddled fans - from soaking wet gloom to a sudden sense of relief and optimism.

This Steve King squad is not perfect, but it has spirit, character, experience. And a drenching night at the Lane is no barrier. Within the next ten minutes, Borough had turned the match irreversibly in their favour with a 3-1 lead.

First, Rees pounded through from midfield, took a touch to get his angle right, and drilled past the visiting keeper for 2-1. The momentum had swung, and the belief was back.

And then it was Rees again - team skipper in every sense, and a man who embodies the spirit of drive and enterprise which his manager is demanding - who extended the lead to 3-1. Carter won the ball from Bangura following a Dulwich corner, and he drove forward with posse of four Borough players, before finding McQueen on the right.

The winger cut across to Rees, whose first effort was blocked before he tucked he ball past Sands at the second bite.

Hamlet really did not know what had hit them. From that bright start, they had seen the match ripped away from them.

The second half brought more of the same. In such buffeting conditions against unpredictable opponents, 3-1 was not necessarily a winning score. Hamlet were looking to sit deep and hit Borough on the counter - and they did exactly that with a swift end-to-end break for 3-2.

Anything Hamlet could do, Borough could do better. Liam Nash - in his first full game since a cheekbone injury - was the man on the mark. Kai Corbett brought down Sam Oguntayo's channel pass with ease, and he drove up the wing before crossing low. Paul McCallum dummied for Nash to steal his fifth goal of the season.

The last 20 minutes saw no further drama. Hamlet brought on the ageless Danny Mills, but even his scoring talents could not retrieve this game for the visitors.

#1966. Antigua and Barbuda vs Trinidad and Tobago - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 10 Nov 2026 10:48, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 11:12

Antigua and Barbuda and Trinidad and Tobago begin their two-legged battle for a place in the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup Prelims when they meet in the first leg of their League A and C Play-In tie at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium on Thursday.

The two sides are competing for a place in the next stage of Gold Cup qualification, with the winner of the tie to be decided over two legs before the return fixture in Trinidad and Tobago on November 16.

Antigua and Barbuda, ranked 162nd in the world, head into Thursday's clash after enjoying a positive conclusion to their CONCACAF Nations League campaign, finishing top of Group B in League C with nine points from four matches.

Jacques Passy's side began their campaign with a 1-0 defeat away to Aruba, but responded impressively by recording consecutive victories over Anguilla, winning 5-0 at home before securing a 3-0 success on the road.

The Benna Boys then completed their group fixtures with a 3-2 victory over Aruba at the start of October, with Sean Tomlinson and TJ Bramble giving them a two-goal advantage before Brandon Satchell scored a late winner.

That result means Antigua and Barbuda have won their last three matches, scoring 11 goals and conceding just twice during that run, and will be hoping to carry that momentum into their two-legged tie with Trinidad and Tobago.

However, Passy's side face a considerable step up in opposition, with Trinidad and Tobago having competed in League A and boasting players with experience in both MLS and the Championship.

Trinidad and Tobago, who are ranked 57 places higher than their upcoming opponents at 105th in the world, will meanwhile be looking to respond after a disappointing Nations League campaign which saw them finish fifth in Group A and enter the Play-In round.

Derek King's side collected just one point from their four matches, losing 3-2 to Haiti, 2-1 against the Dominican Republic and 1-0 away to Curacao before playing out a 1-1 draw with the latter in their final game last month.

Luke Phillip scored the opening goal in that match, but the Soca Warriors were unable to hold onto their advantage, with Jordi Paulina equalising for a Curacao side that recently played at the 2026 World Cup.

That result extended Trinidad and Tobago's winless run to 11 matches, leaving King with plenty to address as his side look to book their place in the Gold Cup Prelims.

Despite their recent struggles, the Soca Warriors will enter the first leg as favourites, although they face an Antigua and Barbuda side who have been strong in recent weeks and will be encouraged by their opponents' poor run of form.

The pair will lock horns for the first time in more than 12 years, with Trinidad and Tobago having won 12 of their previous 15 meetings.

Tomlinson, Kylano Isaac, Quinton Griffith and Jahzihno O'Garro are among the defensive options, while Bramble could feature in midfield.

Crawley Town's Dion Pereira featured in that victory and could be involved again, while Satchell will be hoping to earn a starting role after coming off the bench to score the winner.

Ali Kazim Nakhid, Steffen Yeates, Andre Raymond and Kathon St Hillaire have also been recalled, giving King some extra options as he looks to turn around his side's recent form, while Bristol City full-back Rio Cardines is expected to start and earn his 13th international cap.

Dartford made it three through player-manager Greenhalgh just after the half hour. Matthew Hayden made a mess of a clearance and it landed at Greenhalgh’s feet on the edge of the box, and he took a touch to set up a low drive past Carey.

Sandford was determined to keep a clean sheet against his former side as he made another fine stop to deny Rees. Max Sheaf’s cross from deep was pinpoint and met the head of an onrushing Rees. From just six yards, Rees thought he had pulled one back, but Sandford reacted sharply to parry out and behind.

It was the same old story just before half-time as another mistake allowed Fiddes to make it four. A poor pass led to a one-on-one opportunity with Fiddes against Hayden, and Dartford’s forward outmuscled Borough’s number two, before firing into the bottom corner.

The Sports looked for a response in the second 45 as they dominated possession against a stubborn Dartford block. They had to be patient for chances, but just felt it was not their day as they hit the woodwork again. Corbett’s free-kick panicked Sandford but smashed against the bar.

There was a consolation for Borough, and a fitting goal on his return for Nash. Fellow substitute Terrell Egbri’s cross was helped on by Shay Harrison towards Nash, and after miscuing a first attempt, he produced an instinctive scorpion kick into the roof of the net.

However, even with the momentum on their side, Borough couldn’t grab any more goals back.

#1964. AC Milan Women 0-3 Inter: Chances squandered and a silly red card

Milan Women failed to replicate the heroics of the men’s team in the Derby della Madonnina, conceding three goals against Inter after a silly red card.

After the odd-goal defeat to Como last night time out, Milan Women were out for revenge this afternoon, and perhaps also a little inspired by the men’s win in the derby last weekend. However, Suzanne Bakker’s side made life very difficult for themselves.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Milan actually had a couple of good opportunities to take the lead and make it a very different game. After just four minutes, the veteran Christy Grimshaw got a good chance in the box, but failed to connect with the cross from the left with her head from close range.

About ten minutes later, Mawa Sesay picked up on a loose ball after a mistake by Inter’s backline. However, she somehow missed the target and didn’t even force the goalkeeper to a save, effectively squandering a 1v1 by rushing the shot.

In the second half, the game remained fairly even but one moment proved costly for Milan. As Benedetta Glionna made her way into the box, the aforementioned Grimshaw made her evening worse with a little kick, resulting in a penalty for the away side (somewhat cheap, but fair).

Haley Bugeja made no mistakes from the spot, firing a great shot straight down the middle to give her side the lead in the 57th minute. Milan then began their pursuit of an equaliser after that but instead of a goal, around five minutes later, Sandra Ogalla was sent off.

The goalkeeper used her hands a little bit too early, touching the ball outside the penalty box, and the referee immediately spotted it. Bakker made use of the VAR challenge, prompting the referee to have a look at the screen, but the decision was upheld. A silly red card indeed.

Deputy goalkeeper Sally Rainey was brought on but just a few minutes later, Inter doubled their lead through Glionna. It was a well-worked move, in fairness, but the defending could have been better at the far post. That was in the 67th minute.

Milan tried to get back into the game but struggled with only ten players. And so, in the 83rd minute, Inter were awarded another penalty. This one was even cheaper than the first, as Angelica Soffia barely touched the player.

Despite another VAR check, the decision was upheld and Bugeja bagged her second of the night. That concluded the night from a goalscoring point of view, and Milan Women suffered their second consecutive defeat.

David Bates has received a shock Scotland call-up for the first time in seven years after head coach Sebestien Pocognoli was hit with another key withdrawal in defence.

The former Rangers and Aberdeen centre-back has been capped four times but has not featured for the national team since the opening round of Euro 2020 qualifying back in March 2019.

The 30-year-old has been called into the squad for the Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland as a replacement for Brondby captain Luis Binks, who has been forced to withdraw due to an unspecified issue.

It is the second blow in defence for Pocognoli, who also recalled Los Angeles FC centre-back Ryan Porteous last week after Swansea defender Stephen Welsh dropped out.

Bates' surprise return to the international fold follows a strong start to the Süper Lig season in Turkey with newly-promoted Amedspor, who have surprassed expectations to sit third in the table after 11 matches.

He spent the previous four seasons in Belgium with two years at Mechelen followed by a similar spell at Standard Liege, who sold him to Amedspor in the summer for £420,000.

The Kirkcaldy-born defender started his career with Raith Rovers before earning a development loan move to Rangers which became permanent in January 2017. He left Ibrox just 18 months later to join German side Hamburg where he spent three years which included loan spells at Sheffield Wednesday and Cercle Brugge.

He returned to Scotland to join Aberdeen in 2021 but left Pittodrie the following summer to embark on a career in Belgium.

Bates made his Scotland debut under Alex McLeish in a 4-0 win over Albania in November 2018 and followed this up with his second cap three days later in a 3-2 win over Israel. He also played in the infamous 3-0 defeat in Kazakhstan and the 2-0 win over San Marino in March 2019 before McLeish was sacked the following month.

Steve Clarke drafted Bates into the squad in September 2019 as late injury cover but he was an unused substitute in the defeats by Russia and Belgium at Hampden. Clarke never selected Bates again before resigning after the 2026 World Cup.

#1962. Why it's all gone wrong for Charlton: JAMES SHARPE reveals the summer failures, a player's mysterious disappearance and murmurs of yet another sale as Nathan Jones' side teeter on the brink

Published: 21:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 7 November 2026

Fear is creeping back in at the Valley. Charlton’s defeat by Bolton on Tuesday night, their fourth on the bounce, was greeted with the cacophony of boos it deserved.

Eleven games without a win and teetering above the Championship relegation zone. A fanbase that has been down this long and treacherous road before, and sure as hell doesn’t want to tread it again.

Certainly not when they thought those dark days were, at last, behind them. Only 10 weeks ago, Charlton sat top of the table after victory over Preston completed a hat-trick of early season wins, including a famous triumph in front of a record Championship attendance of 62,264 at West Ham.

It was a false dawn. For the first time under Nathan Jones, the ship has stalled and, for now, is going backwards.

Charlton looked destined for relegation to League Two for the first time in their history when Jones took over in February 2024. They went 14 games unbeaten and survived. After spending eight of the previous nine seasons in the third tier, he took them up via the play-offs at the next time of asking and, last season, kept them in the Championship.

For a club that had endured so much instability, a period of normality and steady progression was on the cards. Jones is Charlton’s ninth managerial appointment since June 2016. Only now, the wonder is how much longer this can go on before nine becomes 10.

Fear is creeping back in at the Valley with Charlton 11 games without a win and teetering on the brink of the Championship relegation zone

For the first time under Nathan Jones, the ship has stalled and, for now, is going backwards

‘If I hadn’t done what I’ve done at this football club, it would have been an easier decision for them (the owners),’ Jones told South London Sport this week. ‘I have to win football games. Win games or you don’t survive.’

His next chance is against ninth-placed Sheffield United this Saturday afternoon. Jones insists he maintains a strong relationship with the Charlton board. The new chief executive Ben Mansford – formerly of Leeds, Blackpool and Barnsley and who ended the club’s spell of 19 months without one – twice tried to hire Jones at his previous clubs. Jones is understood still to have the backing of his players.

Perhaps it’s not best to let him know that both Alan Pardew and Chris Powell lost their jobs after defeats by the Blades.

‘We've spent a lot of time in League One recently and I think there is a kind of head-in-hands worry at the moment: please let's not go back there again,’ Heather McKinlay, chair of the Charlton Athletic Supporters' Trust tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘At the moment, it feels more like duty than fun. I think we have become a little bit worn down because we've been through the mill so much with the changes of ownership and the shenanigans over the near 20 years since we were in the Premier League.’

They have been through the mill, much of the difficulties driven by those in charge. Former owner Roland Duchatelet, who still owns the Valley and the training ground, once accused fans of wanting the club to fail. Charlton’s fans responded to his comments and mismanagement by carrying a red coffin to the Valley followed by a crowd of mourners in a mock funeral protest against his ownership.

They lobbed hundreds of plastic pigs on the pitch for one game, beach balls to halt another, and sent a black cab to Belgium as a ’Taxi for Roland’.

Within weeks of Duchatelet selling Charlton to businessmen Tahnoon Nimer and Matt Southall for £1, the two new men were embroiled in a bitter public row. Nimer accused Southall of using club money to fund his own lifestyle, which he denied, including renting a £150,000-a-year flat in London and giving a fleet of Range Rovers to his associates. Charlton fans occupied the boardroom in protest. Thomas Sandgaard, the next owner, was arrested by the FBI this year and charged with fraud. He denies any wrongdoing.

The highly impressive win away to West Ham in August now appears to have been a false dawn

Jones is Charlton's ninth manager in the last 10 years - but how long can he keep this up?

‘Charlton fans are a proactive lot,’ adds McKinlay. ‘If they feel they can make a difference, they’ll do something. I don’t feel we can do anything right now other than cheer them on. I think the ownership want the club to succeed. The manager wants the club to succeed. The players want the club to succeed. There's not really a baddie in this.’

As one club insider put it this week, it’s nice, in a strange way, that football is the main issue for once and not what’s going on off the field.

There is still a sense of that, mind. The current ownership group known as Global Football Partners is made up of seven shareholders, each with more than five per cent, but it remains unclear who is the driving force. Sources suggest some are more willing than others to put their money in with murmurings that the club is once again up for sale. Charlton insist they are merely looking for more investment to help drive the club forward.

Poor recruitment has not helped matters either. All the talk in the summer was about ‘evolving’ from a team that could get out of League One, then stay in the Championship, to one that could compete.

The club, however, spent a net total of just £1.5million this summer. They failed to find the right winger they needed, as a deal for Crystal Palace winger Jesurun Rak-Sakyi collapsed late on. Instead they signed teenager Junior Nkeng, who hasn’t played a single minute. A lack of creative midfielder is glaring too.

As for those who did arrive, Millenic Alli infuriated supporters in the defeat by Bolton when he headed the ball blindly into no man’s land during stoppage time with the team desperately searching for an equaliser. Nathaniel Chalobah arrived as a free agent from Sheffield Wednesday with a reputation for being injury prone. He showed his class at the start of the season, got injured, returned and is now injured again.

That’s not to mention the bizarre mystery surrounding midfielder Timothy Ouma. The Kenya international, on loan from Slavia Prague, went off to play for his country during the recent break and has not been seen since. Ouma, who has not featured in a single matchday squad since the break, has previous for this, having also failed to return after international duty while on loan at Lech Poznan.

When Jones was asked about it a few weeks ago, he responded by saying: ‘We will address those rumours when they become relevant. Anything we need to put out, we will put out.’

Kenyan midfielder Timothy Ouma went off to play for his country during the recent break and has not been seen since

Nathaniel Chalobah (right) arrived as a free agent from Sheffield Wednesday with a reputation for being injury prone. He got injured, returned and is now injured again

Charlton remain tight-lipped on whether Ouma is still absent, though one insider admitted they still hadn’t seen him since the players returned from international duty. The Kenyan FA did not respond to requests for clarification.

It makes the decision to part ways with club captain Greg Docherty in the summer look even more misguided, with this a team lacking in leadership. Jones has been left to throw all the pieces up in the air and see where they land with constant changes to the team and the line-up. Selection and formation roulette, as some are calling it.

The Welshman is not everyone’s cup of tea, frequently mocked for his David Brent style, but there’s still a belief, not least from himself, that he can turn things around. ‘He’s a maverick, but he’s our maverick,’ laughs McKinlay.

Time is running out, though, because if Charlton cannot find their way again, the alternative is already too unnerving to think about.

#1961. Navalcarnero vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 10:51, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 10:53

Real Betis will be bidding to avoid a shock elimination in the first round of the Copa del Rey when they tackle fourth-tier outfit Navalcarnero on Thursday evening.

The fixture had originally been due to take place at the end of October, but it was postponed following the tragic train crash in the province of Toledo, Spain.

Navalcarnero's best-ever performance in the Copa del Rey came in 2020-21, when they managed to reach the last-16 stage of the tournament, while a spot in the second round was also secured in 2025-26, but Real Betis are standing in their way this time around.

There is no question that the Red and Whites are the huge underdogs heading into this match, but their situation will be helped by the fact that Real Betis will be missing a number of senior players due to international commitments.

Larry Perez's side play their league football in Spain's fourth tier, and the Madrid outfit have never operated higher than Spain's third tier.

Navalcarnero will bring a four-game unbeaten run into this match, winning twice in the process, while they have only lost one of their last eight fixtures.

The Red and Whites currently sit seventh in their domestic table, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and two defeats to collect 16 points.

Real Betis, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 victory over Elche, with the result leaving them fourth in the La Liga table on 26 points.

Manuel Pellegrini's side are also playing in the Champions League this season, sitting 11th in the overall table, having picked up nine points from their opening four matches.

The Seville outfit have the small matter of a league derby against Sevilla after the international break, before travelling to Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League three days later.

Real Betis have won the Copa del Rey on three previous occasions, lifting the trophy in the 1976-77, 2004-05 and 2021-22 campaigns, and they are expected to make an impression in this season's competition given the quality and strength of their squad.

However, El Glorioso have not managed to progress past the quarter-finals of the tournament since lifting the trophy in 2022.

Navalcarnero have not reported any injury problems for this match, so the hosts could have a full squad available for the Copa del Rey fixture.

Kensly Vazquez has scored three times in 12 appearances this season and is expected to operate through the middle for the Red and Whites in this contest.

There should also again be a spot in the side for Peque, who has netted twice in nine appearances in all competitions this term.

Real Betis, meanwhile, will be missing first-team players Alvaro Valles, Manu Gonzalez, Angel Ortiz, Facundo Bernal, Alvaro Fidalgo, Marc Roca, Nelaon Deossa, Abde Ezzalzouli and Troy Parrott for the cup fixture due to international call-ups.

Meanwhile, Cucho Hernandez is still out with a calf injury, so head coach Pellegrini will be without the services a number of senior players for the fixture on Thursday night.

That said, a strong team should still include the likes of Marc Bartra, Dani Ceballos, Pablo Fornals, Antony, Isco and Rodrigo Riquelme, while teenager Jose Morante could be given the nod down the middle.

Calado; Fernandez, Rodriguez, Larranaga, Esteban; Ortiz, Cruz; Lopez, Peque, Alvarez; Vazquez

Conde; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Firpo; Fornals, Ceballos; Antony, Isco, Riquelme; Morante

This is a very tough match for Navalcarnero, and we are expecting Real Betis to comfortably secure their spot in the next round of the Copa del Rey.

#1957. UEFA Nations League 2026-27: How do suspensions work? Yellow and red card rules explained

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 11:17, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 11:18

The league phase of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will conclude in November 2026.

The League A quarter-finals, and League A/B and B/C playoffs will then take place in March 2027, ahead of the Finals in June 2027, and it is set to be a fascinating conclusion to the tournament.

However, players run the risk of suspensions for key matches.

Here, Sports Mole explains how 2026-27 Nations League suspensions work, including the rules surrounding yellow and red cards in the tournament.

In the 2026-27 Nations League, a player is automatically suspended for one match after receiving two yellow cards in separate matches during the league phase.

A second yellow in a separate match therefore equals a one-game ban, while a fourth yellow and a sixth yellow would carry further one-match suspensions.

A straight red card or two yellow cards in the same match means that the player would be automatically suspended for their next match in the tournament.

However, a straight red card can potentially result in a longer ban, depending on the seriousness of the offence, which would be looked at by UEFA.

"As a rule, a player or team official sent off by the referee is automatically suspended for the next match in the competition. In the event of a serious offence, the UEFA disciplinary bodies are entitled to augment this punishment, including by extending it to other competitions," says Article 60 of the Regulations of the UEFA Nations League.

Under the 2026-27 rules, the accumulation of yellow cards will continue from the league stage into the quarter-finals, but after the quarter-finals, the remaining yellow cards are wiped.

As a result, heading into the semi-finals and final, there will be no accumulation of previous yellow cards, so at this stage, only a red card would lead to a suspension.

The Denmark international looked to have ended his long spell without a goal in Sunday’s victory over Kilmarnock at Celtic Park, latching onto Benjamin Nygren’s layoff before slamming home beyond Nico Mantl. However, his delight was short-lived, with the strike disallowed for a foul by Mika Baur in the build up.

Speaking to the Scottish Football Social Club, pundit Michael Stewart isn’t 100 per cent convinced the goal should have been chalked off, saying: “I have a certain degree of sympathy for Celtic and Mika Baur here,” when asked by host Darrell Currie how “desperate” Hogh is for a goal. “It feels like its [the foul] far enough back, that you could maybe let it go?” he added. “Technically it probably is [a foul]. But is that what you want to see for goals getting chalked off?

“As I said, there was a still a bit [of play] before the goal. I’m a bit conflicted with it, because I wanted to see goals scored. But then technically it probably is a foul. So I think the question that needs to be asked is it a high enough bar for it to be ruled out? It is probably right on the bar. He kicks his foot, rather than the ball. Ultimately it hasn’t affected the result, which is a positive. But I’m conflicted. I’m right on the fence with that one.”

Following the game, Celtic manager Martin O’Neill defended the misfiring hitman, saying: “I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did. He is not [Camilo] Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

“Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him. This lad has scored goals in the Champions League, remember. He will get a confidence boost from last night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal.”

Despite O’Neill’s defence of Hogh, and Stewart’s own sympathy for his goal against Kilmarnock being disallowed, the TV pundit thinks that the big number nine will need to start scoring for O’Neill’s men, or accept being replaced by others within Celtic’s squad, with the Scottish champions having plenty of alternatives in their ranks.

“It is going to be a constant concern for Celtic in regards to Kasper Hogh and his performances,” said Stewart. “They have alternatives they can utilise, but when you’re spending that money on a record signing and they’re not performing, it is always going to be a major concern.”

#1954. Derided Thierno Barry is no longer a source of frustration as star fires Everton to victory over Coventry on another big night for David Moyes amid Jack Grealish drama

Published: 17:29 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 06:27 EST, 7 November 2026

Maybe Everton should request to play under the lights every week. It certainly seems to push David Moyes' team to new heights.

Following hot on the heels of consecutive night victories over Newcastle United, Friday's 3-1 win against Coventry City was a reminder of why, under Moyes, there is renewed sense of optimism at Everton.

Up to fifth, above Liverpool, and in a Carabao Cup quarter-final at Fleetwood, it could prove to be a special season.

This always felt like a big task for Frank Lampard, back at Everton for the first time since his sacking in 2023.

Popular as the ex-manager may be, there's no room for sentiment, certainly not from Moyes on a night he took charge of his 592nd game, drawing level with Harry Catterick for managing the most games in the club's history.

He'll set it outright after the international break against Brentford and Keith Andrews, who was 21 when Moyes first took up the reins at Everton.

Thierno Barry (right) now has 10 goals this season after being widely derided in his first season on Merseyside

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall had been left out of the England squad in the morning, but refused to let it spoil his night

His side started impressively, fashioning three shots in the opening 10 minutes, before losing all momentum and allowing Coventry into proceedings.

It took going 1-0 down, to a soft Yann Gboho goal, for the hosts to come alive. Thierno Barry, so often the source of frustration last season, was magnificent and all but won the game with a five-minute brace in the second half.

The striker didn't score his first goal until December last season. This campaign, he's reached 10 before the second international break. Moyes joked post-match that Erling Haaland should watch his back in the Golden Boot race is starting to feel less absurd. Barry now sits joint second in the charts.

Both goals against Coventry came via back post-duels. The first he confidently headed past Carl Rushworth, before bundling in a second five minutes later.

The disgruntled home fans booed the team off at half-time, yet were jubilantly cheering and signing after Barry's brace. The Frenchman danced on the pitch at full-time and was serenaded by the South Stand.

'I don't see loads of young centre-forwards scoring loads of goals in the Premier League,' said Moyes.

'He's come in and has settled in a bit more. His language and communication is better and obviously he's worked to get himself into the positions to score.'

Barry wasn't the only Everton goalscorer, of course. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was not one of the three Everton players named in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday - only Arsenal had more representatives.

EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 5; Rohl 5 (O'Brien 73min, 6), Tarkowski 5, Branthwaite 6 (Keane 89), Mykolenko 6; Armstrong 6 (Hackney 73, 6), Garner 6; Dibling 5 (Johnson 73, 5), DEWSBURY-HALL 8, George 5 (Alcaraz 90); Barry 8.

COVENTRY CITY (4-2-3-1): Rushworth 4; van Ewijk 5, Mfuni 6, Pinnock 6, Dasilva 6; Yirenkyi 6, Torp 6 (Grimes 86); Sakamoto 5 (Tchaouna 86), Rudoni 5 (Hamer 86), Gboho 6 (Thomas-Asante 73, 5); Awoniyi 5 (Cherif 87).

But the midfielder sent a pointed message to the Three Lions' boss with a superb showing that was capped with a late powerful goal to end the contest.

'It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie,' Dewsbury-Hall told Sky Sports after the game. 'It's a massive dream to play for my country. I know I was close.

'Yeah, sad, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up. I've got the mentality. I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens.'

'He's desperate to play for England,' added Moyes. 'You never know if England get a couple of injuries, or anything changes.'

What ended as a comfortable win could have been a different outcome had Jame Tarkowski been punished for a hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi, or if Vitalii Mykolenko's tussle with Taiwo Awoniyi in the box had been deemed a foul.

Both were checked and cleared by VAR, as was a handball claim in the build-up to Barry's second goal.

'Tarky pulls on Caleb's hair, they [VAR] are saying it's not enough of a pull,' said an aggrieved Lampard afterwards. 'That's a hard area to be in. What is hair pull and what's not?

'I think Taiwo, on the edge of the box was a penalty. I feel there's a penalty by the time Myko's knee is in the back of Taiwo's knee on the line of the box.

'Then the Barry one is handball. He flicks it in [with the hand] with the final touch. Nothing went for us tonight.'

#1952. ‘Without doubt’ – Lack of physicality major reason behind Crawley Town’s league position, says interim boss

Having been at the club for three weeks, Blackwell has had ample opportunity to assess the Reds squad.

And the former Leeds and Sheffield United once again highlighted Crawley’s deficiencies.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

He said: “We are neither technical or physical. We are not a totally technical side or a totally physical side.

“We brought Ben [Heneghan] in who is a 6ft 3 centre half, we brought Connor [Wickham] at 6ft 2 up front – we need some more physicality.

“In central midfield we have nobody above 5ft 8. You look at the games against Tranmere and against Oldham, they were physically towering above us yet we’ve shown we have the capabilities to fight.

“It’s not all about just having big boys, it’s about having the desire and the fight to make sure that you win your battle.”

Blackwell also reiterated his concerns surrounding the club’s recruitment.

He added: “Once again, I question the recruitment. If you have six people in midfield and the tallest is 5ft 10 and three are 5ft 8, how do you deal with a 6ft, 6ft 2 midfield player?

“We’ve got to look at balancing the physical and technical side. I see us at the moment being half of one and half of the other and it’s not working.”

League Two is an extremely physical division – and Blackwell admitted the Reds were being ‘bullied’ by opposition teams.

He said: “Without doubt we are getting bullied on the ball. Everybody knows what League Two football is

“We’ve got to look at areas of the pitch we need to be strong – and that’s ironically in both boxes, and then the flare in the wide areas”

“At the moment we haven’t got that so we are trying to address that and that’s what the owners are trying to do.

“We need to try and get through to Christmas and then see if we can maybe change the dynamics of the squad – but knowing full well what is required in this league.”

Following Blackwell’s thorough assessment of the squad, he was rest assured that the board will take on his advice and make the changes required to steer the club away from trouble.

He said: “I think they are well aware themselves of the situation. You’ve only got to watch the games to know that physically we’ve struggled against teams that are more physical than us.

“You bake a cake and the recipe has got to be right. It’s not all about height, it’s also about technical ability, speed, power.

“But every sport is power and pace. We haven’t got enough of that at this moment in time, but we’ve recognised that and are trying to correct it.”

Crawley have signed four free agent in the past fortnight. Now with a squad of 32, Blackwell has the challenge of sorting through the squad and picking his best 11.

He said: “First of all you look at attitude and you look at ability and you look at what they do in training everyday. Tthat’s a big for any coach what they do on the training ground, and that can influence your decision.

“I’ve seen these now for two weeks. I’ve seen them on the training ground, I’ve now seen them in the game and all my experience in the game tells me I know what they can do and what they can’t do.”

The Reds now have an extended break before their next game, having had this weekend’s game against Rotherham postponed.

When asked how he would tackle this next week, Blackwell said: “The great thing about football is everyday is different and problems arise out of nowhere sometimes, but the good thing for the next few weeks is that we’ve got no game in hand.

“We can now concentrate on the training ground. We are focussing on Fleetwood and how we are going to try and get a result against Fleetwood.”

#1949. Sunderland injury news: Granit Xhaka fitness update provides reason for Stadium of Light concern

By Carter White | 10 Nov 2026 11:59

Sunderland midfielder Granit Xhaka has withdrawn from international duty with Switzerland this month.

The 34-year-old started on Sunday afternoon in the top flight for Regis Le Bris's side as an Enzo Le Fee penalty was enough to secure maximum points over Chelsea, however, the Black Cats are still 19th in the Premier League standings.

Xhaka lasted just four minutes of the North-East contest before being replaced, with Sunderland going on to defeat the visiting Blues, who were again without the services of star striker Joao Pedro.

After the opening 10 matches of the Premier League campaign, Le Bris's troops have collected just eight points, sitting only above crisis-hit Crystal Palace in the rankings as a relegation battle looms large.

Sunderland will be looking to record back-to-back top-flight victories for the first time this season following the international pause on November 21, when they make the tricky trip to Aston Villa.

Speaking on social media, the Swiss FA have confirmed that Sunderland midfielder Xhaka has been withdrawn from international duty this month, representing a major blow to both his club and country.

The post reveals that the 34-year-old's problem is a calf issue, with the former Bundesliga champion set to miss UEFA Nations League clashes with Slovenia and Scotland over the next week.

When quizzed on Xhaka's issue following the Chelsea win, Sunderland boss Le Bris said: “It looks like a calf injury, but we do not know exactly the timeframe at the minute. It was just the last sprint of the warm-up, that is often the case [with these injuries].”

The ex-Arsenal man had a scan on his injured calf yesterday with the results yet to be revealed, however, the fitness setback is clearly large enough to keep him sidelined over the next fortnight.

Murat Yakin's Swiss side have enjoyed a marvellous start to their Nations League B campaign, winning four consecutive matches in the September/October window to give themselves the opportunity to secure promotion with a victory in Slovenia on Friday.

After featuring in 99 competitive games for Bayer Leverkusen over a two-year period, Xhaka arrived at the Stadium of Light during the summer of 2025, helping Sunderland to reach new Premier League heights.

The veteran midfielder featured in 36 games across all competitions for the Black Cats as they avoided relegation with ease, instead securing a spot in this season's edition of the Europa League.

In the twilight of his career, it is no surprise that niggling injuries are beginning to hinder Xhaka, who has gone through an enormous amount of midfield work for Leverkusen and Sunderland since 2023.
