#1947. Why England will privately regret missing out on Scott McTominay - 'he wasn't saying anything about them'

When Jose Mourinho first alerted Alex McLeish to the possibility of securing Scott McTominay's international allegiance, little could he have imagined the midfielder would become one of Scotland's most influential players.

The former Manchester United manager wanted to know if McLeish was aware McTominay was eligible to represent Scotland. That conversation proved the starting point of an international career that has become hugely beneficial to the national team.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McTominay's return to the Scotland squad earlier this week, following heart surgery, for the final Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland represents a major boost for new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli, who will welcome the availability of such a talismanic figure early in his tenure.

For McLeish, however, the Napoli midfielder's inclusion rekindles memories of the international tug-of-war that could so easily have ended in England's favour.

The Three Lions were also interested in 2018, but Scotland were determined not to miss out on a promising young talent at Old Trafford. McLeish recalls travelling south during the ‘Beast from the East’ to watch McTominay first-hand, where his physical presence and technical ability immediately caught his attention.

However, it was McTominay’s emphatic response when offered the chance to pull on the dark blue jersey that ultimately settled the matter.

“Everyone will read this and be saying ‘there he goes again!’ But it was amazing to get him,” McLeish admitted. “Word was in the air about Scott and Jose phoned me and said ‘you know this boy can play for Scotland?’ And I said, ‘I do now!’ I then organised to go down to see him. He was still just a kid, quite raw. But he had the physique, speed and skill on the ball. He was good in the air and also with the ball at his feet that made it a no-brainer.

“The only problem we faced was that England were in the frame as well. But when I said to Scott, ‘I'd love you to play for Scotland,’ he said ‘That's the only nation I want to play for.’ And all of a sudden we had a brand new young superstar.”

The value of that decision has become increasingly apparent. McTominay has developed into a commanding international presence, combining physical strength, technical ability and a natural eye for goal from midfield.

Initially deployed in defensive positions, including centre-back, he has since made his mark further up the pitch, with his ability to drive through midfield and time his runs into the penalty area becoming a major asset.

“It's incredible how he's grown and grown,” McLeish said. “In the first few games he was just trying to feel his way into the international scene. But Scott gave everything from that first call-up. He's played in just about every position in the team down the years. He was in the back four at one stage. But he's mainly operated in the middle of the field and he's a real threat in the box and moving from middle to front.

“The way he runs with the ball is just superb because he really knows what he's doing. He's got massive confidence and I hope that a lot of young Scottish players coming into the game can take inspiration from what Scott has done.”

There is also the question of whether England have been left to rue a missed opportunity. Having come through Manchester United's academy, McTominay was a player England could realistically have pursued. However, Scotland's willingness to offer him a clear international pathway was ultimately rewarded.

McLeish suspects the decision will not have gone unnoticed south of the border. stating: “They have such a massive pot to pick from in England. But I'm sure that privately, in some of their chats behind the scenes, they will have said ‘we should have got McTominay.’ But he chose Scotland. He wanted to come. He wasn't saying anything about England at all. And that was the best news I could have got in that era of rebuild.”

McTominay's return provides a timely boost for Pocognoli as he looks to put his own stamp on the national team. Having an established performer of his calibre available will be a significant advantage for the new head coach.

McLeish knows the difficulties of international management when key players are unavailable. During his own spell in charge, he recalls travelling to Kazakhstan with several important members of his squad missing.

“It'll be a massive relief for the manager to get Scott back into the squad. You always want your best players available. I remember back in my day, going out there and we were held in a bit of limbo. So for Pocognoli to get players into his team of that level will be massive for him. It could make a huge difference for Scotland.”

#1946. 'People keep telling me it's great I'm managing against my son... it's not - it's horrible': Peterborough boss ROBBIE SAVAGE and Reading star CHARLIE on their 'awkward' FA Cup showdown, playing for Man United and dangers facing modern young players

Published: 02:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EST, 7 November 2026

The FA Cup cast its spell upon the Savages while they were out shopping for groceries.

Reading midfielder Charlie was strolling the aisles of the Marks & Spencer foodhall with his girlfriend when his phone began to buzz. He remembered it was first-round draw day.

He fished out the phone, saw the cascade of messages and realised, as they like to say in M&S, this was not just any FA Cup draw. He called his dad.

Peterborough United boss Robbie was in the Co-op. He had stopped on his way back to the rented lodgings he describes as a 'little annexe in someone's garden' and was rummaging through the ready meals in search of a spaghetti bolognese for one when he answered.

'The reception in Peterborough isn't great, it kept cutting out,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Charlie said: "You won't believe the draw." I thought he was going to say Forest Green. Or Macclesfield. I didn't think about Reading. He said: "You've got us." I just went: "Oh no."'

They were on a collision course from the moment Robbie left Forest Green for the Posh job last month. The teams were scheduled to meet in League One next month at Reading but the FA Cup draw caught them off guard.

Peterborough boss Robbie Savage (right) with his son, Reading midfielder Charlie. The pair will meet in the FA Cup first round at London Road on Saturday

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport

And while they were both at great pains to stress that Saturday's tie at London Road, screened live on TNT Sports, is about Peterborough and Reading not their little family gathering, they can appreciate the fuss.

'Football is a beautiful game, it brings people together and creates rivalries,' says Charlie. 'This week it's created a rivalry in our family. I'm not sure who my mum, brother, grandparents and cousins will support but there's no better time for them to have a half-and-half scarf.'

For Robbie, the beauty of the occasion is yet to unfurl itself. 'It's going to be horrible,' he says. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling. People keep telling me it's great. I've got to say it's not great, it's horrible. Usually we speak every day and I've not been able to speak to him all week because I don't want to put him in a position where anything gets out and anyone can point a finger at him.

'I don't want it to be billed as Savage v Savage because it's not. Charlie might not play but if he plays and makes a mistake and we score the winner, so be it. If he plays and scores the winner, well, wow.'

Robbie puffs out his cheeks and widens his eyes as he considers this scenario. 'We've got to win for Peterborough United,' he adds.

Ironically, it was a passion relit by coaching his sons which tempted the former Leicester, Birmingham and Blackburn midfielder out of the comfort of his media work and into coaching. Savage helped out with his youngest son Freddie's Under 13s team in the Timperley and District Junior Sunday League.

'Standing out at training on a Tuesday and Thursday night,' says Robbie. 'Sunday morning, putting the nets up. I've been that dad. In the first season we were hammered 13-0, but we built a team and won a lot of things.'

Charlie Savage in action for Reading. The midfielder played 45 games for the club last season but has yet to start a league match during this campaign

Savage offers some advice to his team in his new role as manager of Peterborough

Two years ago, Charlie and Freddie implored their father to follow his heart and make the switch from sporting director to manager at Macclesfield in the Northern Premier League.

'Even back then, he said one day he'd manage against me,' Charlie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I was in League One and he was in Step Three and I'm thinking, "Well, give it a few years", but he always gets where he wants to get to.

'He's a competitor. He wants to win, wants to succeed. Even with my little brother's team it hurt him to lose in Sunday morning grassroots football. That's something inside him and it won't change.

'He will want to beat us. Unfortunately for him, I'm the same. I want to win. There might be an awkward car journey home.'

Charlie's memories of his father playing football are from Derby, the last stop of a 15-year professional career which started at Manchester United and took in seven different clubs, as well as 39 Wales caps. 'I remember seeing his long hair, scurrying around the pitch,' says the 23-year-old. 'Throwing his arms up and shouting at the refs.'

Like his dad, Charlie also came through United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

'He'll always have that on me,' says Robbie. 'All I ever wanted to do from 14 to 19 was play for one minute in Manchester United's first team. It didn't happen and he's done it. His name is on the wall at Carrington and mine isn't.

'I'm so glad his name is there instead of mine. You want the best for your sons. I'm proud of both my sons.'

Charlie has three Wales caps and counting. His father won 39...

...but despite both Charlie and Robbie coming through the Manchester United academy, only Charlie played for the first team (above), against Young Boys at Old Trafford in 2021

Freddie is studying for an economics degree at the University of Manchester. Charlie left United for Reading four years ago and now has 175 senior appearances and three Wales caps under his belt and a reputation in his own right.

'He's got a great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie. 'He's intelligent. Nine As in his GCSEs. He doesn't drink, he lives his life 24 hours a day, seven days a week to be a footballer. He's a down-to-earth, humble kid.

'He was so brave to go and play senior football when he had three years left at Manchester United, and it's paid off. He played 45 games last season. He hasn't started a league game this season but hasn't sulked.

'I was a sulker, as Martin O'Neill and Nigel Clough (who coached Savage at Leicester and Derby respectively) will tell you. If that was me, my body language would be negative, but he's got a great attitude. And I've tried to tell him now he has to train harder than ever and conduct himself in the right way.'

If Robbie is a guiding light and inspiration for Charlie, vital information flows both ways for an aspiring manager with a young team.

'The mindset of a Millennial is completely different to when I played,' says the 52-year-old Posh boss. 'If they're not in the team or the manager has shouted at them, they go home to an apartment where they live alone away from their families, isolated from 2pm to 7am with all that time to think about it.

'We have to understand their vulnerabilities on and off the pitch. Charlie has been through that so without knowing it, he's made me a better manager. I try to think about what's best for my players, what I'd want a manager to do for Charlie in that situation.'

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end,' Charlie says of his dad Robbie

'Great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie of his son Charlie

Being the Son of Sav cannot be easy. Not only the added scrutiny and expectation, and accusations doors have been opened for him by a famous and influential father, but also in a world where footballers are too often considered fair game for abuse whether inside the stadium or online.

'It's there in all forms of life,' admits Charlie. 'Maybe people subconsciously want me to fail a little bit more because of who he is. I get it. Football is a game and my dad is a divisive figure inside that game.

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end. Sometimes the abuse goes too far. People forget he's a human not just a football personality.

'But I wouldn't change who he is. I wouldn't change having him as my dad, I'm very proud of him.'

#1945. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!

It seems like Milan is biggest own enemy in last couple of seasons. To predict this match is basically to predict how they are going to enter into the game.

Team must go for the win because this season and today position is opening opportunity to reach top positions.

Milan will win this game but again depend on the rotation. Personally I think why Milan can’t play consistently because of the heavily rotation. You cant gel into the games if too many changes each every game. They should just change 1 or two every game. Even when you want to rest certain key players. Just substitute them by half time instead.

#1944. Goals and cup drama are plentiful in ESFL

In the Premier Division, Battle Town followed up their victory over Sidley United with an impressive 5-1 win away to Sandhurst.

Jake Warner opened the scoring in the 14th minute before Glen Carrick doubled Battle's advantage midway through the first half. Dean Boyd struck twice after the interval to put the visitors firmly in control, before Sandhurst's James Found pulled a goal back. Boyd completed his hat-trick in the 74th minute to round off another excellent afternoon for Battle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Rye Town maintained their good form with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over The Junior Club Tackleway. Goals from William Brown, Charlie Stevens and Ole Reader secured all three points for Rye.

Sidley United bounced back from their defeat against Battle with an emphatic 5-1 victory over SC Pass & Move Arrows. William James Ray led the way with a brace, while Harrison Smith, Lewis Hole and Darrell Shaw were also on target for the hosts.

Bexhill Amateur Athletic Club continued their impressive goalscoring form with a thrilling 4-3 away victory over Victoria Baptists. The hosts found the net through Thomas Williamson, who scored twice, and Theodore Ridley, but Bexhill did enough to edge an entertaining seven-goal contest and secure another valuable three points.

In Division Two, Parkfield continued their excellent run with a 4-1 home victory over SC Pass & Move Arrows II. The visitors' consolation came from Oscar Ellwood, but Parkfield proved too strong as they maintained their impressive recent form.

Division Three saw Little Common III secure a hard-fought 2-1 away victory over Hollington Hawks. Rafael Dos Santos and Ben Messetter were on target for Common, while George Brooks replied for the hosts. The scheduled meeting between Herstmonceux II and Hawkhurst United was postponed.

Attention also turned to the Sussex Junior Challenge Cup, where Bexhill Amateur Athletic Club II produced one of the performances of the weekend to defeat BN Dons Saturday Reserves 4-3. Trailing 3-1 at half-time, Bexhill staged a tremendous second-half comeback to book their place in the next round. Frankie Deeprose was the hero with a hat-trick, while Ashley Elphick also found the net. Sam Rayner and Torin Seagrove, who scored twice, were on target for the visitors.

Herstmonceux also progressed following a closely contested 3-2 away victory over Eastbourne Athletic, while Pevensey & Westham were involved in a dramatic encounter against Chichester Athletic. The sides finished level at 3-3, but Pevensey were eventually beaten 10-9 on penalties.

There was disappointment for Mountfield United, who suffered a 9-2 defeat away to Ashington Rovers, while Ninfield II were beaten 5-0 at home by AFC Varndeanians Reserves.

In the Hastings FA Intermediate Cup, Wadhurst United and Ninfield played out an entertaining 3-3 draw before Wadhurst secured their passage to the next round with a 5-3 penalty shootout victory.

The Hastings FA Junior Cup also produced plenty of excitement, with Little Common II progressing after a dramatic penalty shootout victory over Battle Town II. The sides finished level at 2-2, with Cyrus Abbott and Jay Abib scoring for Common, while Ryan Southall and James Williams replied for Battle. Common eventually held their nerve to win 5-4 on penalties and secure their place in the next round.

Northiam 75 also progressed after edging past Ticehurst with a 3-2 victory, having led 1-0 at the interval. Joshua Jevon and Edward Harwood were among the goalscorers for Ticehurst.

St Leonards Social and Sedlescombe Rangers served up an eight-goal thriller, finishing 4-4 after normal time. Dan Laidlaw scored twice for Social, with Nicky Croft and David Gautrey also finding the net. Sedlescombe's goals came through Sean Lennard, Spencer Sharkey, Owen Smith and Liam Whicker. Sedlescombe eventually progressed following a dramatic 6-5 penalty shootout victory.

Finally, in the Hastings FA Lower Divisions Cup, Icklesham Casuals continued their excellent recent form with a convincing 4-1 home victory over Robertsbridge United II. Kieron Buss, Declan Eades, George Stoodley and Greg Stoodley were all on target for Icklesham.

Northiam 75 II also secured their passage to the next round with an impressive 3-1 away victory over Sedlescombe Rangers II.
